nearest_prs.read: Body read this session: put a water bottle into a side-entry bike cage under a small frame's top tube, pushing the cage's sprung front arm open until it seats.
nearest_prs.comparison: Shared: a bottle retained by a spring. Theirs is lateral insertion of a light bottle into a fixed cage that flexes open. Ours is a two-stage angled insertion of a 1 kg full bottle up a tilted, hinged holder's axis past sprung jaws, then a swing about the holder's hinge to latch, on a free-standing machine that tips if pushed wrongly; the bottle ends hanging by its neck. Different mechanism, motion and success state.

physical_skill: Lift a 1.05 kg full bottle, tilt it to a forward-hanging holder's 15 degree axis, insert its neck through the lead-in and push it up the axis until the collar cams two 800 N/m jaws apart and drops onto them, then swing the bottle's bottom back about the holder's hinge to vertical so it latches, and let go, without tipping or sliding the free-standing 3 kg machine.
valid_shortcuts: GPU/CPU red team on this task.py: do nothing 0; naive straight-up push 0 (machine tips past 5 degrees); early release before the swing 0.25; holding instead of releasing 0.5. The latch requires the collar in the jaws, so swinging the empty holder upright scores nothing; tipping, dropping or sliding the machine zeroes the trial. Valid solution: the manufacturer's neck-in-at-angle, push up and back (demo 1.0 twice). Dream-1 this session: 0 (right gripper came to the bottle's side but never grasped or lifted it).
